description: A prolapsed umbilical cord can reduce or stop blood flow to your baby and lead to brain injury or death. Your doctor or midwife must manage it immediately.
shortAnswer: A prolapsed umbilical cord can result in a reduction or complete stop of blood flow to your baby and lead to brain injury or death. It is the responsibility of your doctor or midwife to manage a prolapsed cord immediately.

faq.q: How is a prolapsed umbilical cord managed during delivery?
faq.a: A prolapsed cord can be managed quickly by moving the baby away from the cord or delivering the baby quickly or if necessary by caesarean section. If it is managed quickly there will be no permanent injury.

faq.q: Does a delay in managing a prolapsed cord increase the risk of brain injury?
faq.a: The longer the delay, the greater the chance your baby will suffer a brain injury or die. Proper management of a prolapsed cord is critical to prevent permanent harm to your baby.
